title: The Crown of Ashvale Revisited
premise: Wendell Blackwood, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead through her carvings, has survived the Thornfell mountains by keeping her gift secret and guiding smugglers along paths no living map records. When the crown of Ashvale declares a hunt for the gifted—blaming them for a plague of restless corpses—Wendell is captured by a zealous inquisitor who needs her talent to find the true source of the dead's unrest: the buried crown of Ashvale's first king, which whispers to anyone who listens. As Wendell is forced deeper into the mountains she thought she knew, she discovers the dead are not rising in anger but fleeing something worse—an ancient pact sealed beneath Thornfell that the old royal line paid for with an entire generation's souls. To end the hunt and silence the crown, Wendell must choose between destroying it and claiming it, knowing that whoever wears its authority over the dead will be bound to the mountain forever. In the end she shatters the crown on the thirteenth turn of the moon, freeing the dead at the cost of her own hearing—and walks out of Thornfell carrying the last whisper as a promise rather than a burden.
about_author: Rosalind Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing funerary carvings in remote mountain parishes before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about ordinary people whose small magics carry unbearable weight.

chapters.title: The Listening Bone
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In her workshop above the smuggler town of Greyhollow, Wendell finishes a memorial carving for a drowned child and hears his final words. The beat establishes her gift as both comfort and curse, and her careful life of secrets.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Pass
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A smuggler client warns her that crown riders burned a bone-shrine two valleys over and posted a bounty for 'hearers.' Wendell weighs flight against the winter stores she cannot abandon. The beat is dread creeping into routine.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Warrant
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Crown riders led by Inquisitor Serah Vane raid Greyhollow. Wendell's apprentice betrays her under questioning, and Vane arrests her—not to kill her, but because the dead near Thornfell have stopped resting, and Vane needs a hearer. Beat: betrayal and reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Dead Refuse to Say
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Chained in a supply wagon, Wendell tests Vane by reading a dead soldier's token; what she hears terrifies even her—the dead are running from something beneath the mountain, not toward vengeance. Beat: the mystery deepens beyond politics.

chapters.title: Thornfell Gate
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The expedition reaches the walled mining town of Thornfell Gate, where grieving families press relics into Vane's hands. Wendell reads one relic publicly to buy goodwill and hears a name no one alive should know. Beat: her secret becomes leverage.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. An old royal cartographer, Odo Fenwick, joins the party with maps of passages sealed since the founding war. He recognizes Wendell's knowledge of the smuggler roads and quietly offers her escape—if she'll steal a page from Vane's orders first. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: A Page Torn Twice
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell steals the order and learns the crown already knows about something called the First King's Crown and intends to claim it, not destroy it. She burns the page but keeps the knowledge. Beat: complicity; she chooses to stay for answers.

chapters.title: Voices in the Deep Road
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Descending through sealed galleries, the party's lanterns fail and the dead speak through every loose stone. One voice calls Wendell by her grandmother's name. Beat: the personal history entwines with the ancient horror.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. They find a cavern of carved bones arranged like an audience chamber—a place where hearers once served the crown openly. Wendell realizes the hunt is erasing her own lineage's history. Beat: grief and fury at institutional erasure.

chapters.title: Vane's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Serah Vane. Vane reveals her sister was a hearer executed in the last purge, and that Vane joined the hunt to control it from inside. Her faith in the crown cracks. Beat: antagonist becomes tragic mirror of Wendell.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn Begins
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Astronomers in the party confirm the moon enters its anomalous thirteenth turn, when the old pact's binding weakens. Restless dead grow desperate, clawing toward the surface. Beat: clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weeping Stair
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Crown deserters turned corpse-raiders ambush the expedition; Wendell uses the dead's own fear to turn them aside, revealing her full power to everyone. Beat: exposure—she can no longer pretend to be a mere tool.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. To save the wounded, Wendell bargains with a dead queen's echo, offering a year of her own memories. She wakes having forgotten her mother's face. Beat: the theme lands—survival always costs something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: Odo's Treason
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Fenwick steals the recovered map fragment and flees toward the crown's capital to sell the crown's location. Vane wants pursuit; Wendell argues the crown itself must never reach the capital. Beat: alliance strains toward breaking.

chapters.title: The Pact Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. At the threshold vault, murals show the truth: the first king bought victory in the founding war by pledging a generation of souls, and the crown is the seal. The dead aren't rebels—they're collateral, waking as the pact decays. Beat: revelation reframes everything.

chapters.title: Crown or Key
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The dead queen's echo offers Wendell the choice: wear the crown and command the dead justly, or break it and free them into oblivion. Vane, arriving wounded, begs her to break it; Fenwick's distant torches signal the crown's agents closing in. Beat: moral climax staged.

chapters.title: The Weight of Authority
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Wendell lifts the crown and, for one terrible moment, feels every dead soul in Thornfell lean on her will—and understands how easily justice becomes ownership. She sets it down. Beat: power refused at its most seductive.

chapters.title: Shatterturn
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. On the final night of the thirteenth turn, Wendell, Vane, and the freed dead hold the vault against the crown's soldiers while Wendell strikes the crown with her carving hammer. It breaks; the dead sigh out like a long-held breath. Beat: climax and sacrifice—her hearing dies with it.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. In the aftermath, Wendell grieves the loss of the voices that were both torment and companionship. Vane burns her warrant and vows to report the crown destroyed and the hunt unjustified. Beat: mourning transformed into peace.

chapters.title: The Long Way Home
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. The survivors climb out of Thornfell as spring thaw opens the passes. Wendell guides them not by the dead's whispers now, but by memory and chalk marks—her craft reduced, her freedom intact. Beat: quiet reclamation of ordinary skill.

chapters.title: Greyhollow Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Back home, Wendell confronts the apprentice who betrayed her and chooses mercy over exile, then faces the town that sold her out. Some doors stay closed; others open. Beat: justice outside the law, administered personally.

chapters.title: The Last Whisper
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. Carving a simple memorial months later, Wendell hears one faint voice—the dead queen's echo, kept behind as a promise that the freed souls found rest. She smiles, pockets her chisel, and steps into the market crowd. Beat: resolution with wonder; the price paid was worth it.
